messages:
sarah: Heads-up — Customer ACME reported spikes in 503s and token throttles on their Dedicated pool since 09:12 UTC. They say traffic is hitting the wrong pool and we see elevated queueing.

 tom: @sarah can you paste the request headers and the control-plane route decision logs? also which tenant and pool?

 sarah: Tenant: acme-prod (tenant_id=acme-77). Pool observed: dedicated-gpu-xlarge-2 but expected dedicated-gpu-xlarge-primary. Route log snippet:
```
2026-03-15T09:11:58Z DEBUG route-eval tenant=acme-77 headers={"X-Redwood-Tier": "[gold, beta]", "X-Customer-Tags": "team:search"} selected_pool=dedicated-gpu-xlarge-2 reason="tier-match"
```

 nora: hmm header shows tier as a JSON-ish array string. We recently changed the header parser to accept CSV. could be parsing order or trimming bug. :thinking: 

 sandeep: @nora iirc the control plane normalizes to first-match and maps tier->pool via priority list. if the parser yields `"[gold, beta]"` instead of `gold,beta` the mapper treats it as single unknown token => fallback mapping picks pool by fallback priority (which in this tenant's config currently points to xlarge-2).

 ops-oncall: Paging the runtime team — this is causing sustained throttles for acme. Oncall metrics: 4.2x token latency and 60% of requests queued in front of xlarge-2 GPU. Can we confirm a regression deploy around 09:00?

 support-bot: deploy-bot: rollout/ctlplane-parser v3.7.1 deployed at 2026-03-15T08:58:12Z to controlplane/eval

 tom: that's the suspect deploy. @sandeep can you repro locally with header payload variants? quick repro steps would help customer support/ops.

 sandeep: repro steps I used:
 1) curl -v -H 'Authorization: Bearer <token>' -H 'X-Redwood-Tier: "[gold, beta]"' https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate
 2) watch controlplane logs for route-eval entries

 Observed: the parser emits the entire string as single token: `tiers=["[gold, beta]"]` which maps to fallback pool. When header is `X-Redwood-Tier: gold,beta` it maps correctly.

 nora: confirmed locally. The parsing change in v3.7.1 accepted bare arrays but didn't strip bracket chars when header came from legacy SDKs that stringify arrays. Patch: trim leading/trailing [ ] and quotes before split. I'll prepare PR.

 sarah: Customer wants ETA and temporary workaround — can we advise them to set header to CSV, or apply tenant override to map fallback to correct pool?

 tom: short-term: advise CSV header or add tenant-level override for acme-77 to point fallback->xlarge-primary. longer-term: revert parser change or hotfix.

 ops-oncall: I've applied tenant override for acme-77 to force pool affinity to dedicated-gpu-xlarge-primary. Monitoring: queue depth dropping within 2 mins. :white_check_mark:

 sandeep: pushing hotfix branch now, will run e2e then deploy. PR: controlplane/parse-tiers-fix, tests added for quoted-array headers.

 nora: PR approved, deploy scheduled to canary at 10:05 UTC. I'll follow up with release notes and add a migration note for SDKs.

 sarah: Customer informed and relieved. They implemented the CSV workaround in their proxy. Will follow up tomorrow for postmortem and permanent config change.

 tom: recap for postmortem: cause=header-parser regression in v3.7.1, effect=tenant fallback -> wrong pool -> noisy neighbor throttling. mitigations=tenant override applied, CSV workaround recommended, hotfix PR and canary deploy. Action items: add header-parsing unit tests, add telemetry alert for unexpected single-token tiers, update SDK docs.

 support-bot: ticket #INC-2026-ACME created and linked to this thread.

 sarah: thx everyone. closing loop once canary stable. :pray:
